title: Adverbs: how, when and where things happen
examples: Do all adverbs end in ly?

figure.question: What does the adverb tell you?

explain.say: Picture a tortoise walking. Now picture it walking slowly. The word slowly tells you how it walks. Words that describe a verb are called adverbs. Look at the how box on the board: slowly, loudly, carefully.

draw.text: Adverbs: how, when and where things happen

explain.say: Look at the board: slow plus ly makes slowly. Many adverbs are made by adding ly to an adjective. Quick becomes quickly, soft becomes softly. Can you turn loud into an adverb?

draw.note: adjective plus ly makes an adverb

explain.say: Watch out for words ending in y. See the first chunk, happi? The y changes to i before ly, so happy becomes happily. Can you do the same with angry?

draw.name: x-word
draw.note: y changes to i before ly

explain.say: Not every adverb ends in ly. Look at the when box: now, yesterday, soon. They tell you when something happens. We are going to the market soon. When did you last eat a mango?

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: What does the adverb tell you?

explain.say: Last box: where. Here, outside, upstairs. The cat ran outside. Well done, adverb expert! Challenge: make one sentence with all three: Yesterday, my dog ran happily outside.

draw.question: What does the adverb tell you?

faq.a: An adverb is a word that tells you more about a verb: how, when or where something happens, like slowly, soon or outside.

faq.q: Do all adverbs end in ly?
faq.a: No. Many do, like quickly, but now, soon, here, very and often are adverbs too.

faq.q: How do I turn happy into an adverb?
faq.a: Change the y to i and add ly: happy becomes happily. Angry becomes angrily the same way.
No, friendly is an adjective even though it ends in ly: a friendly dog. To say how, use in a friendly way.
asks: Words ending in ly that are not adverbs

faq.a: It is an adverb or adverb phrase moved to the start of a sentence, followed by a comma: Slowly, the tortoise crossed the road.
asks: Adverb at the start of a sentence

facts: Adverbs can also describe adjectives, as in very tall, and other adverbs, as in quite slowly.
Friendly, lovely and lonely end in ly but are adjectives, not adverbs.

quiz.say: Which word is the adverb? Mei sang loudly in the hall.
quiz.show: Which word is the adverb? Mei sang loudly in the hall.
quiz.why: Loudly tells you how Mei sang.

wrong.1: sang is the verb that loudly describes.
wrong.2: hall is a noun, a place.

quiz.why: Tomorrow is a time, so it answers when.
